review.brief: Review RM28 tier 3 (RM28-battery-derive-consumed-per-day) in internal/battery + cmd/poller. Diff range 732df05..HEAD. VALIDATE: (1) module-boundary compliance - battery must not reach another module's DB or internals; cmd/poller is the only place battery->telemetry is orchestrated (D4a), telemetry must never call battery. (2) D18 CONFORMANCE, the highest-value check: bucketing must use CapturedDate-1 in the poller's zone; telemetry.Snapshot.EffectiveDate must NEVER be read as data anywhere in internal/battery. The owner overruled a UTC design once already - confirm it did not creep back. (3) The D13 formula sums over BOTH charge sources with neither taking precedence; D12 matching is source-specific (Supercharger by instant interval on charge_stop_date_time, manual by charged_on); D5/D5a detection incl. the named minFlagDistanceKm constant; D8 spans. (4) TEST-CONTRACT RULE: the tests must assert design.md's Test Contract expected values, authored BEFORE implementation - not whatever the code happens to do. T4.10 is the D18 regression test and the only case distinguishing the ruled-on rule from the overruled one; verify it genuinely fails if bucketing regressed to EffectiveDate. Tests were written by a DIFFERENT worker than the implementation, deliberately. (5) LEADER DEVIATION TO WEIGH (decision D8): T6 is a reconcilingCollector decorator on telemetry.Collector, NOT design.md's verbatim inline snippet. Rationale: Scheduler.Run calls CollectAll internally so cmd/ had no seam for the scheduled path, and the literal snippet would have reconciled only under --once. Judge whether the decorator is correct and whether a telemetry hook would have been better despite D4a. (6) cmd/ has NO test files anywhere in this repo, so T6 ships untested by that convention. Judge whether that is acceptable here or a real gap. (7) Performance-Profile compliance (read-heavy) and the anti-gaming checks: no weakened acceptance criteria, no self-approved statuses. TEST-EXECUTION-POLICY: Claude writes tests but never runs the suite. Judge test QUALITY BY READING them - do not run them. Signals: go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt and openspec validate --strict were ASSISTANT-run and all clean. The go test suite pass and the cmd/poller run were BOTH USER-REPORTED by the owner, never claimed by the assistant.

Independently verified: (a) diff 732df05..HEAD touches only internal/battery/, cmd/poller/, cmd/README.md, and openspec/ -- no other module edited; (b) EffectiveDate is never read as data anywhere in internal/battery -- only appears in doc comments and the one deliberate T4.10 fixture that sets it to a wrong value to prove the regression guard works; effectiveDay(s) derives strictly from CapturedDate; (c) D13 sums both sources via sumSuperchargerPctBetween + sumManualPctBetween with neither taking precedence, matching design.md and spec.md scenarios; (d) D12 matching is source-specific and boundary-correct ([from,to) on ChargeStopDateTime instant; (fromDay,toDay] on calendarDay(ChargedOn)); (e) minFlagDistanceKm is a named const, never inlined; (f) D8 span handling emits exactly one entry per span dated the later snapshot's effective day, no entries for intervening days; (g) go build/vet/gofmt -l on every touched file and openspec validate --strict all independently re-run clean; (h) cmd/README.md and battery/AGENTS.md updated per docs-track-change; (i) progress.json tasks/decisions/events show no evidence of weakened criteria or self-approval -- every task append-only, T4/T5/T6 correctly held at awaiting-user-verification until the owner's reports (D7, D9) flipped them to done. sumManualPctBetween calls the pre-existing manualcharge.Entry.BatteryDelta() helper instead of inlining the Start/EndBatteryPct nil-check design.md showed -- verified BatteryDelta() is byte-identical in semantics (nil if either nil, else End-Start) to what design.md specified; this is a legitimate reuse of an existing public helper, not a deviation of substance.
